notes:
A clean courier quest: one giver, three deliveries, one return. Step 1 hands out FOUR key items, but only the Seal of the resistance is used as evidence -- each captain's linkpearl is handed over and gone the moment you reach him, so an AND-list over all four would read false after the first delivery for no gain. The Seal survives until Ayame takes it back at the end, which is exactly the span the ladder needs it for. Nothing after step 1 is observable: losing a linkpearl is not something a packet reports, so steps 2-4 carry their linkpearl as a REQUIREMENT (what you must be holding) and no evidence.

The page lists Argus, Helga and Rashid in route order (Conflux #03, #05, #02) but never says the order matters, and all three linkpearls are in hand from the start -- so they share a group and all three draw at once. A strict ladder would mark Argus and hide the other two until you happened to visit him. The grouping is inferred from the shape of the quest, not stated by the page, which is why it is flagged.

The deliveries are recorded as 'trade' rather than 'talk' even though the page words them 'Speak to': holding that captain's linkpearl is exactly the 'ready to hand in' condition the kind exists to express.

notes:
The page disagrees with itself about the Hyacinth stratum abyssite: the header lists it as the Reward, while walkthrough bullet 2 says you receive it when you agree to participate, BEFORE any of the four fights. Hard rule 7 is a bright line -- an item in the header's Reward proves the quest is over, not that a step is done -- and nothing on the page settles which reading is true, so the abyssite is evidence on NO step. (Verify pass: the draft put it on step 1; that has been nulled.) The cost of nulling is nil -- the ladder falls back on the session latch -- while the cost of being wrong was a mark frozen on Owain for the whole quest. The conflict stays flagged and the quest stays medium.

Bullet 3 is one bullet spanning four zones, so it splits into four steps -- one zone each, as the schema requires. They share a group: the page gives no order and the four notorious monsters are independent. Each zone lists three rift locations rather than one spot, so the grids stay in the notes and the steps carry no grid; a Voidwatch rift is opened where you choose, not at a fixed point.

'Quest Reqs: Adventurer's Certificate, Level 75 or higher' is two gates. The level is modelled; the Adventurer's Certificate is a key item prerequisite with no slot in the schema, so it is flagged and gates nothing.

notes:
Three bullets, three steps, and the sub-bullets are all advice: the level 90-95 monsters around the ???, the fact that only the Goblins aggro, and the warning that riding the geyser at (I-8) strips Invisible so Grounds Tome Field Support will fail. None of them is a rung.

The real cost here is weather. The ??? only exists during sunny weather -- meaning no weather at all, no icon -- and nothing in the packets reports weather, so a player standing on the right spot in the wrong conditions will see the marker and find nothing. The page says so plainly, so it is flagged and put in the note rather than pretended away. The ??? sits on the (I-5)/(J-5) boundary; (I-5) is recorded and the boundary kept in the note.

notes:
Nine bullets, five steps. Bullet 1 is the precondition that you zone after The All-New C-2000, not an action. Bullets 8 and 9 sit under a 'Notes:' heading and are flagging conditions -- the quest cannot be started with Windurst Mission 9-2 or The Kind Cardian open -- so they are neither steps nor gates the schema can express; they are recorded here.

Bullet 3 is the one real loss. The page says only 'the Cardian that Kororo mentions' and never names it, so the target is none/null and that step gets no marker. Inventing a name -- the reward-list and later bullets do name a Five of Spades, but that is the one in Buburimu, not this one -- is exactly what would produce a confidently wrong marker. The greeting you pick genuinely does not matter, per the page.

Bullet 4 is one step, not two: leaving the zone and coming back after one earth minute is the gate on talking to Kororo again, and a bare 'wait' rung would carry no target and could not be tracked. Bullet 5 is information that identifies the Cardian in bullet 6, so they merge. This quest has no key items and no items at all, so every step's evidence is null and the ladder runs on the session latch throughout -- which is the honest answer, not a defect.

notes:
A three-step quest with an optional gossip round hung off bullet 1. Those three talks are the page's own '(Optional)' and are for flavour only, so they are optional and share a group -- there is no order to them. The page gives no location for Kororo, Kopuro-Popuro or Boizo-Naizo; they are recorded in Windurst Woods because that is where the bullet they hang under happens, and no grid is claimed.

Bullet 4 is not a step: it is the repeat reward (1,000 gil for another starfruit after completion, with the page admitting it does not know whether that is unlimited) plus a second round of closing lore AFTER the quest is over. A post-completion talk cannot be a rung on a ladder that has already ended, so those four are deliberately dropped rather than modelled as an epilogue.

The page writes 'Cursed Weapons'; the singular is used as the monster name, since a plural cannot match a live entity. The kill is not really the step -- holding a Bruised Starfruit is, which is why it is the evidence: the page says outright the fruit can just be bought at the Auction House, and the ladder is correct either way without needing a branch.
